newsitem.title: JORDAN: Busy parallel market trade underpins Amman stock.
newsitem.headline: Busy parallel market trade underpins Amman stock.

text.p: Jordanian shares were steady at end of weekly trade on Wednesday helped by a large deal in local South Korean Goldstar manufacturer on the parallel bourse for newly established firms, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose a slight 0.04 percent to 152.83 points in low turnover of 318,787 dinars ($450,264).
But the parallel bourse with 947,110 dinars of trade stole the thunder for the second day in a row from the official exchange.

"Most of the activity is on the parallel market while investors in the official market focused on high performing stocks or those which have a link to the parallel bourse," said Mohammed Abdullah, analyst at Pearl Consulting.
Only a handful of stocks saw activity on the official market as institutional investors continued to steer away from the bourse in the absence of new market direction.

National Cable and Wire Manufacturing and Arab Aluminum Industries were the top gainers in the market, underpinned by healthy 1996 earnings. They rose 4.89 percent to 2.79 dinars and 3.64 percent to 3.42 dinars respectively.

Focus on Middle East Complex, a manufacturer of South Korean Goldstar products under licence, was behind the high turnover in the parallel market, which in turn helped lift the otherwise quiet market.
Its deal of over one million shares shares worth 853,584 dinars accounted for most of the business on the parallel bourse. The stock's price closed unchanged at 0.78 dinars.

Buying interest in large industrial concern NAMICO was shown, underpinned by market speculation it plans a capital rise after securing large export orders. NAMICO rose 0.03 dinars to 0.71 dinars in 30,814 dinars worth of trade.
Political uncertainty over Middle East peace combined with a lack of liquidity has recently depressed sentiment and prompted outside buyers and institutional investors to remain on the sidelines.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.12 points to 81.12 points, still 2.72 percent down from the start of the year.
